title: Best Video Ad Creators (2026): How to Hire for Commercials
h1: Best Video Ad and Commercial Creators
description: How to hire a video ad creator: what the package should include, how to brief it, what drives the price, usage rights and red flags.
intro: A video ad has a few seconds to stop someone scrolling, so the first moments and the format matter as much as the footage. Orders go wrong when the size, length or usage rights are not agreed, and the finished video cannot run where you planned. This guide covers what to settle before production starts.

faq.q: Which video sizes do I need?
faq.a: It depends on where the ad will run. Vertical 9:16 suits stories, reels and short-video apps, square 1:1 or 4:5 suits feeds, and horizontal 16:9 suits video sites and websites. Ask for every size you plan to use in the same order.

faq.q: Can I use the video in paid ads?
faq.a: Only if the license allows it. Check that the package covers paid advertising, on which platforms and for how long, especially if the video includes actors, voice-over or stock footage.
Often, but make sure it is licensed for commercial use in ads. Music that is fine in a personal video can get an ad rejected or muted.

faq.q: Should I ask for several versions?
faq.a: Yes, if you can. Ads with different openings, lengths or calls to action let you test what works. Many packages offer extra versions or cut-downs as an add-on.

faq.q: What is the difference between a commercial and a UGC video?
faq.a: A commercial is produced and branded, often with motion graphics, actors or product shots. A UGC video looks like a real customer filming on a phone. Both work in ads; they suit different brands and budgets.
